utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, please, call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84bis-T, The Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Daniela Kravetz, for the Prosecution, together with Priya Gopalan, our legal intern, Andrej Micovic, and our Case Manager, Line Pedersen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Ben Emmerson for Ramush Haradinaj, together with Rodney Dixon, Annie O'Reilly, and Andrew Strong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Emmerson. And for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning. Gregor Guy-Smith, Chad Mair, Gentian Zyberi, on behalf of Idriz Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Richard Harvey, assisted by Mr. Paul Troop, and Mr. Luke Boenisch for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Harvey. And may the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told the Judges yesterday that all of your troubles began when you made statements against a particular named individual in another criminal investigation in Kosovo. Do you remember telling us about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before I forget, Exhibit D204, may it please be kept under seal. May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could I please tender the document that have previously been on the screen. That's 1D120328 in the English and 1D120321 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D120328 shall be assigned Exhibit D205 under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the judgement that we've just been looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, we should in be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to be asking you some questions on behalf of Lahi Brahimaj. First of all, it's right, isn't it, that you have given all of your testimony here in court in B/C/S and not in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not really comfortable speaking Albanian, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, when you gave your first statement to the Prosecution in this case, you indicated that Lahi Brahimaj was addressed by Ramush Haradinaj using the word "dajko"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told the Prosecution that "dajko" is the Albanian word for a maternal uncle; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the word for maternal uncle is "dajit" [phoen] in Albanian, isn't it, or don't you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not "daja" [phoen] it's "daj" [phoen]. Perhaps that would be better. It's not "daja." It's "daj."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's certainly not "dajko," is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dajko" is a form of respect, a term of respect. I've already said why it was "dajko." Just like "bace."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're using a Serbian word and not an Albanian one, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand this. Could you please be a little clearer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just giving an example, Witness, of the fact that you are not comfortable speaking Albanian. You're much more comfortable speaking Serbian, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know Kosovo at all, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you mean, I don't know Kosovo at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we okay saying all this in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I was just trying to stop the witness because I thought we were possibly getting to a point where we should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- go into private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, after further consideration of the record so far, and discussion with my colleagues, I've decided that there are no further questions that I need to put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Harvey. Madam Kravetz, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I have no re-examination for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judges?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I have one question for the witness. Mr. Witness, on Tuesday, you were asked about the incident with the two Roma boys and the Serb boy, what happened once they arrived at hospital with these three men -- with these three young men. Your answer was: "We waited outside. The local soldiers carried them in. After a quarter hour, maybe, they took them out again." And then the question was: "Were the three young boys still alive when they were taken out of the hospital again?" Your answer is: "They were no longer alive." You remember all that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: My question is this: Were you told or did you hear what happened to them for all three of them to die within a quarter of an hour after arriving at what seems to be a hospital? Were they in such a bad shape when arriving at that hospital, or did something bad happen to them inside? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you explain what you know, or tell us what you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you then, and I will repeat now. I can provide an explanation, if I may. When they were taken in, as I've already told you, one of them had his ear cut off. They were black and blue because they had been beaten. They were barely breathing when they were brought in. That's how badly beaten they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you don't know of what -- what happened inside, and you took it as normal that quarter an hour afterwards, they were dead, all three of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have already told you, Your Honour, I was outside. They were taken in, and I don't know what happened inside, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions by the Judge. Madam Kravetz?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just place it on record, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So sorry. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Sir, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you so much for coming to testify. You are now excused. You may now go back home. Don't go stand up yet. We've got to go into closed session before you get out. May the Chamber please move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be heard, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just hold it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just two brief matters of housekeeping, if I may, in relation to the last witness. Firstly, there remain the two statements that were put to the witness in cross-examination as to which there is an issue between the parties as to whether they ought to be admitted, and, if so, on what terms. May we consider our position and potentially liaise with the Prosecution and return to the Trial Chamber in relation to them? Secondly, a significant though not, I hope, undue amount of this witness's testimony took place in private session. Given the nature of the evidence, and its importance, we are going to invite the Trial Chamber to release most of what took place in private session subject to careful redactions, and so we will in due course - and I hope sooner rather than later - be filing with the Trial Chamber an application to release into open session a large part of what took place in private session with names and places redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Madam Kravetz?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We'll deal with those matters when -- when counsel raise them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Madam Kravetz, what are we going to do next?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Rogers will be addressing Your Honours on that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as you know, there remains one witness, Witness 80. There are no other live witnesses that presently will be called by the Prosecution. Your Honours have before you an application to amend the 65 ter list in relation to one additional witness. Subject to that ruling, there will be no further live evidence in this case. Your Honours, perhaps it's appropriate to go into private session briefly whilst we deal with the situation concerning Witness 80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Given the situation in which we find ourselves, the Chamber will stand adjourned to the 13th of February, unless we hear sooner about Witness 80, in which case a hearing will be scheduled. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 13th day of February, 2012, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.58 p.m.,
